definition: A contractual relationship — romantic, business, or hybrid — structured entirely within corporate legal frameworks, granting both parties limited shared benefits and protections only while employed by the same corponation. Dissolves automatically upon termination of either party's contract.
origin: Corporate HR jargon from Sterling-Nakamura's benefits restructuring of 2171, now used sardonically in common speech
usage: Mid-tier workers, HR drones, and cynics commenting on corponation life
example: Don't get sentimental — it was a scaffold marriage from day one. The moment Axiom cut her division, we were already strangers on paper.
